Message from the Executive Director
I am delighted to share with you the Bi-Annual Work Programme of the SESAR 3 Joint Undertaking
for the period 2026-2027. These two years will be decisive for our partnership, marking the final
stretch of the current Multi-annual Financial Framework and offering the opportunity to continue
delivering on our current mandate while preparing the future of both our partnership and of the
European ATM research and innovation.
Developing digital solutions for the modernisation of Europe’s ATM system remains our core business.
After years of development, the projects launched under the first Digital European Sky calls will start
to deliver mature SESAR Solutions aligned with the European ATM Master Plan. At the same time, we
will launch the final exploratory and industrial research calls (ER4 and IR3) in 2027, ensuring a
continuous flow of technological solutions through the SESAR innovation pipeline, from low to high
technology-readiness levels.
Equally crucial will be their deployment. A major milestone will be the submission to the European
Commission of the proposal for a Common Project 2 (CP2) in 2026, the regulatory instrument for
implementing Strategic Deployment Objectives (SDOs) through a synchronised and harmonised roll-
out across Europe, translating the research results achieved over recent years into measurable
improvements in network performance, resilience and sustainability.
As we advance along this path, the SESAR 3 JU will continue to act as a bridge connecting research,
innovation and deployment, and uniting all actors of the European ATM ecosystem around a shared
vision. Through this collective approach, we ensure that innovation translates into operational reality
while strengthening Europe’s global influence by promoting interoperability, harmonisation and the
competitiveness of our ATM industry. The planned expansion of the partnership to include members
from third countries associated to Horizon Europe will further reinforce this dimension.
Today, modernising Europe’s ATM is a strategic imperative. Without faster development and
deployment of SESAR Solutions, growing congestion, higher emissions and increasingly fragmented
and vulnerable airspace risk undermining Europe’s competitiveness, technological sovereignty and
climate objectives. Achieving the collectively agreed ambitions of the European ATM Master Plan will
require sustained commitment and mobilisation across the aviation community - from research and
industry to regulators and ANSPs - and I count on our members to maintain their active engagement
in turning this vision into reality.
This work programme represents a collective commitment to make Europe the most efficient and
environmentally friendly sky to fly in the world. You can count on me and on the SESAR 3 JU’s
dedicated staff to deliver it.
Andreas Boschen
Executive Director SESAR 3 Joint Undertaking

Chapter I – Introduction
1 Our Mission
The SESAR (Single European Sky ATM Research) project is the technological pillar of the Single
European Sky (SES), which seeks to reform the European air traffic management (ATM) system and
improve its performance. The SESAR 3 JU coordinates the definition and development phases of the
SESAR innovation cycle and facilitates the market deployment of SESAR Solutions. It builds upon the
experience of the SESAR Joint Undertaking and the successful implementation of the SESAR 1 and
SESAR 2020 R&I Programmes. The goal of the SESAR 3 JU is to deliver the Digital European Sky (DES),
a vision seeking to transform Europe’s aviation infrastructure enabling it to handle the future growth
and diversity of air traffic safely and efficiently, while minimising environmental impact. This will make
air transport smarter, more sustainable, connected and accessible to all civil and military airspace
users, including new entrants.
The SESAR 3 JU’s mission statement is “to accelerate through research and innovation the delivery
of an inclusive, resilient and sustainable digital European sky”:
• accelerate – reducing the time to market through focused and agile R&I, supporting
faster transition to deployment through an extended innovation life cycle;
• inclusive – integrating and connecting all types of air vehicles and users, including civil
and military, manned and unmanned;
• resilient – enabling flexible, scalable, safe and secure ATM that can withstand
disruptions in the aviation system;
• sustainable – establishing Europe as the most efficient and environmentally friendly
sky to fly in the world.
SESAR’s vision is to make Europe the most efficient and environmental friendly sky to fly in the
world. By doing so, the SESAR 3 JU not only delivers on the SES priorities, but also contributes actively
to the overarching EU policy objectives of the “European Green Deal”1 and the “Sustainable and

2.1 The European ATM Master Plan: our roadmap to the Digital European Sky
The SESAR 3 JU is in charge of the stewardship of the European ATM Master Plan, including its
updates6 and the monitoring of the SESAR project. The 2025 edition of the European ATM Master
5F
Plan7 represents a bold and ambitious vision for the future air traffic management in Europe. It calls
6F
for a strong focus of the entire sector on market uptake activities, through Strategic Deployment
Objectives (SDOs) (Figure 1).
Figure 1: Strategic Deployment Objectives (SDOs)
The SDOs, 10 in total, are based on SESAR Solutions already delivered or in the pipeline and address
essential operational changes covering ATM functionalities, including a new service delivery model,
that need to be rolled out between 2025 and 2035. Focusing on these 10 SDOs and ensuring the
timely deployment and operational integration of SESAR Solutions is the path to achieve the Digital
European Sky. The ATM Master Plan also introduces Development Priorities (DPs) that focus on the
exploratory and industrial research required to deliver new technological solutions aligned with the
performance ambitions of the SES. The 12 DPs cover the prioritized actions needed to develop future
ATM functionalities and roll-out phase D (Figure 2), supporting the long-term vision of where we want
the sector to be by 2045.

Phase D of the ATM Master Plan introduces several challenges, including the need to integrate higher
levels of automation and connectivity, further transition to trajectory-based operations (TBO),
implement dynamic airspace management, and integrate new and green aviation technologies such
as zero-emission aircraft, all while keeping the role and function of human operators central. The ATM
Master Plan recognizes these as pressing R&D challenges that require addressing cybersecurity risks,
ensuring seamless multi-link communications, and integrating innovative air mobility (IAM) solutions
like drones and air taxis into an already complex airspace. The objective is not only to enhance
operational efficiency and safety but also to ensure that Europe's air traffic system evolves in a
sustainable and secure manner, meeting both environmental goals and growing traffic demands.
Achieving this vision will demand the commitment and collaboration of all stakeholders, to make
Europe the most efficient and environmentally friendly sky to fly in the world and keep it at the
forefront of global air transport.
2.2 The Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda
The Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda (SRIA)8, developed in preparation of the DES
7F
Programme, sets out to the initial framework linking the ambitions of the SESAR 3 JU to the EU’s
Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) and the Horizon Europe Programme. The SRIA identified
flagships and roadmaps for their implementation. As the ATM R&I landscape continues to evolve, the
ATM Master Plan 2025 includes a mapping between the SRIA’s flagships and the development
priorities (DP) to ensure coherence and alignment at all strategic levels.
3 Strategy for the implementation of the supporting R&I programme
The DES programme is structured into three main R&I phases: exploratory research (ER), industrial
research and validation (IR), and digital sky demonstrators (DSD). The SESAR 3 JU operates through a
holistic and interconnected innovation pipeline, based on these three R&I phases, comprising a
continuous cycle of definition, development, and deployment phases. This integrated approach
allows the seamless progression of ideas from exploration and conceptualization (low TRL) to real-
world application.

The pipeline is constructed from four categories of activities; categories 2 and 3 are within the
industrial research and validation phase:
1. exploratory research (TRLs 0–2), funded under Horizon Europe for the EU part;
2. industrial research and validation (TRLs 3–6), funded under Horizon Europe for the EU part;
3. fast-track innovation and uptake (TRLs 2–7), funded under Horizon Europe for the EU part;
4. Digital Sky Demonstrators (TRL 8), funded under the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) for the
EU part9, in collaboration with CINEA.

The SESAR 3 JU provides financial support, mainly in the form of grants, to R&I indirect actions,

Chapter II – Bi-Annual work programme for 2026-2027
1 Executive Summary
In 2026–2027, the SESAR 3 Joint Undertaking (SESAR 3 JU) will continue to monitor and steer the
implementation of the Digital European Sky (DES) programme ensuring its alignment with the
priorities and ambitions of the newly adopted European ATM Master Plan. These two years will be
decisive, as they cover the final phase of Horizon Europe and set the ground for the next programming
period post-2027. In this context, the Bi-Annual Work Programme (BAWP) 2026–2027 defines the
priorities and activities to ensure optimal success, focusing on nine operational objectives that
capture the main achievements expected at operational and organisational levels.
Operational activities
In 2026, the SESAR 3 JU will deliver a major milestone with the submission to the European
Commission of the proposal for a Common Project 2 (CP2). This cornerstone instrument, once
brought forward by the European Commission, will support the implementation of the ATM Master
Plan through a synchronised and timely deployment across Europe of the SESAR innovation that
support the transition to a more efficient and future-proof ATM system.
The JU will continue to ensure a strengthened monitoring and strategic steering the implementation
of its portfolio of projects across all 3 phases of the innovation pipeline. Since the waves of projects
launched in the first half of the programme (ER1, ER2 and IR1 calls for proposals) will reach their final
phase, SESAR 3 JU will ensure that they deliver their Solutions at the expected level of maturity, and
will conduct their orderly closure. In addition, it will finalise the selection and launch into execution
the projects under the ER3 and IR2 calls (launched in 2025), and will prepare the final DES calls namely
ER4 and IR3 to be launched in early 2027. Projects under the IR2 and IR3 calls will develop the
Solutions addressing Phase D of the ATM Master Plan.
The SESAR 3 JU will continue to facilitate and support the acceleration of market uptake of the SESAR
Solutions by providing technical expertise in the implementation of the ongoing DSD projects
(DSD1a–DSD3), and will contribute to the preparation of a potential DSD4 call to be launched in 2026.
In addition, the JU will coordinate with EASA and EUROCAE to ensure that the technical regulatory
framework supports the implementation of the deployment priorities defined in the ATM Master Plan
with a particular focus on the roll out of the SDOs and the transition to a new service delivery model.
Synergies and collaborations with a wide range of stakeholders will ensure that the R&I activities are
embedded within a broader European, national and regional agenda, leveraging investments,
avoiding duplication, and ensuring coherence between research, innovation, and deployment.
Particular efforts will be dedicated to strengthen the cooperation with the European Space Agency
(ESA) notably through a memorandum of cooperation.
ATM being global by nature, the SESAR 3 JU will continue to engage and collaborate with international
actors, notably in the context of ICAO, to ensure global interoperability and a harmonised framework.
In particular, it will implement targeted measures to mitigate global harmonisation risks associated
to the elements in scope for CP2. In addition, the JU will expand its partnership to include new
members established in third countries associated to Horizon Europe.

Support to operations
To deliver on these ambitions, the SESAR 3 JU will continue to provide a range of corporate and
support services to ensure operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and organisational
resilience. Building on the Back Office Arrangements with other JUs and administrative collaboration
with the European Commission and EUROCONTROL, the SESAR 3 JU will pursue further efficiency
gains across its processes. At the same time, it will maintain a lean internal structure, operate as an
agile organisation, remain an attractive employer, and advance its transformation into a greener and
more digital workplace through the implementation of action plans on the introduction of Eco-
Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS) and for its digital transformation.
Communication and outreach will remain a key enabler, with activities aimed at promoting the DES
vision, raising awareness of projects results and SESAR Solutions, and demonstrating the central role
of the SESAR 3 JU in the orchestration of the ATM ecosystem. To that end, the JU will organise yearly
events such as the SESAR Annual Conference and the SESAR Innovation Days, and will participate
actively in major EU and international events.

2.2 Activities per Strategic Areas of Operations
2.2.1 Strategic area of operation 1: Provide strategic steering to the Digital European
Sky programme

a strengthened monitoring of the development and deployment activities in line with the European

the current programming period.
Transversal projects launched under the IR1 (AMPLE3 and PEARL) and IR2 calls will help steer the R&I
efforts of the SESAR 3 JU. Their support will mainly focus on the European ATM Master Plan
monitoring notably through the Strategic Deployment Monitoring Report and the support to the CP2
definition. In addition, the transversal projects support the DES programme execution, notably
through community-building, project progress assessments and performance evaluation of the SESAR

2.2.2 Strategic area of operation 2: Deliver exploratory research
This SAO addresses the first phase of the SESAR innovation pipeline which aims at bringing out
innovative, unconventional and breakthrough solutions through exploratory research covering both
fundamental (TRL 0-1) and applied research (TRL 1-2). Activities under this SAO will contribute
towards the objectives of launching the new wave of projects, and ensuring the delivery of the SESAR
Solutions in line with the Master Plan priorities. This will be achieved through the monitoring and
steering of projects funded under the calls for proposals ER1, ER2 and ER3, to ensure that the
Solutions developed reach the expected maturity gates and are aligned with the Development
Priorities and the ATM Master Plan roll out milestones. The subsections below summarise the planned
activities per call.
DES ER 1 call (HORIZON-SESAR-2022-DES-ER-01)
In 2023, 18 grants have been awarded as a result of the ER1 call, amounting to a total EU contribution
of € 22 million, for a total investment of around € 25 million. These projects have completed their
research activities in Q3 2025 and will be closed by the end of Q1 2026, except for the transversal
project Engage 2, which will continue its activities into 2027. In 2026, the SESAR 3 JU will support the
final phases and orderly closure of these projects, and consolidate their results.
DES ER 2 call (HORIZON-SESAR-2023-DES-ER-02)
In 2024, 18 grants have been awarded as a result of the ER2 call, amounting a total EU contribution
of around € 26 million, for a total investment of around € 28 million. The implementation of these
projects started in Q3 2024, with closure of the research activities expected in Q3 2026, and project
closure in the first half of 2027. Throughout 2026-2027, the SESAR 3 JU will closely monitor these
projects to ensure that research activities are conducted in accordance with the signed grant
agreements, particularly regarding timelines and deliverables. Additionally, it will ensure that the
developed Solutions align with the Development Priorities of the ATM Master Plan and reach the
expected maturity level.
DES ER 3 call (HORIZON-SESAR-2025-DES-ER-03)
On 15 January 2025, the SESAR 3 JU published the ER3 call, which opened on 1 April, with a call
deadline on 16 September 2025. The call amount of € 24 million is divided between WA1 on
Fundamental research (€ 10 million to cover the Development Priorities FR-1 to FR-3), and WA2 on
Applied research (€ 14 million to cover the Development Priorities AR-1 to AR-3). In 2026, the SESAR
3 JU will finalise the grant preparation process in view of signing the grants by mid-May. The SESAR 3
JU will closely monitor these projects during their implementation to ensure the delivery of the
Solutions aligned with the ATM Master Plan and at the expected maturity level before the end of the
research activities by mid-2028.
DES ER 4 call (HORIZON-JU-SESAR-2027-ER-04)

In 2026-2027, the SESAR 3 JU will prepare and launch the last exploratory research call under the DES.
The ER4 call will aim at selecting projects that should deliver Solutions addressing strategic
development priorities for fundamental research (TRL 0-1) and applied research (TRL 1-2) as defined
in the ATM Master Plan. During 2026, the SESAR 3 JU will develop the technical specifications which
are expected to be adopted by the GB in December of that year. The ER4 call will be tentatively
opened in January 2027 with a call deadline set for May 2027. Following the evaluation and the award
of the selected proposals, the grant preparation phase should be open in September, leading to the
signature of grant agreements before the end of 2027 and the beginning of the research activities in
early 2028. Execution of the research activities will run until the end of 2029.
The indicative budget of the ER4 call is not yet known.
2.2.3 Strategic area of operation 3: Deliver industrial research and validation
This SAO addresses the second phase of the SESAR innovation pipeline which supports the transition
of potential SESAR Solutions to maturity levels of TRL6 or 7 (for fast-track projects). In 2026-2027, the
SESAR 3 JU will focus on the delivery of the Solutions needed to advance Phase D of the European
ATM Master Plan. Therefore, the main objectives during these two years will be the launch of the last
wave of DES calls, in particular the IR3 call, and the delivery of the SESAR Solutions in line with the
Master Plan priorities. This will be achieved through the monitoring and steering of projects funded
under the calls for proposals IR1, EU-RAIL – SESAR Synergy and IR2, to ensure that the Solutions
developed reach the expected maturity gates and are aligned with the Development Priorities and
the ATM Master Plan roll out milestones. In addition, the activities will include a gap assessment of
Phase D as part of the preparations of the IR3 call for proposals to be launched in 2027. During these
activities, particular attention will be paid to the early engagement of the projects with the EASA
(safety, regulatory, standardisation and certification aspects where appropriate). The subsections
below summarise the planned activities per call.
DES IR 1 call (HORIZON-SESAR-2022-DES-IR-01)
32 grants have been signed in Q3 2023 with a total granted amount of around € 181 million, for a
total investment of around € 347 million. The SESAR 3 JU will focus on the final phase of the
monitoring of these IR1 projects to ensure that they deliver their SESAR Solutions aligned with the
Development Priorities at the expected maturity level in the first half of 2026. The projects will be
closed in 2026.
Synergy call with EURAIL (HORIZON-ER-JU-2023-FA1-SESAR)

2.3 Research and innovation priorities, challenges and expected impacts
The challenges facing the aviation sector are both longstanding and emerging. Most critically, the
sector must significantly reduce its CO emissions while managing an ever-growing volume of air
2
traffic, which will continue to strain the capacity of the ATM system. Over the coming decade, the
usage of the airspace will undergo significant changes, making it more complex to manage with the
introduction of new types of air vehicles, such as drones, air taxis, and high-altitude aircraft. By 2035,
zero-emission aircraft (e.g. hydrogen and electric) that may operate differently from today's
traditional aircraft may begin entering service. These transformations must be addressed in the
context of increasingly severe weather caused by climate change and a shifting security and defence
landscape in Europe, which not only poses additional security challenges but also reduced the
available airspace by around 20%. In light of these challenges, the ATM system will need to become
more scalable, resilient, and efficient, leveraging digitalization and automation to enable optimal
flight trajectories across the network, anywhere and anytime.
Against this backdrop, the European ATM Master Plan 2025 sets the vision and priorities to make
Europe the most efficient and environmentally friendly sky to fly in the world by 2045. It also outlines
the expected benefits (capacity, fuel, CO , punctuality, cost-efficiency) as well as what that means for

Europe’s economy and citizens. This vision is underpinned by the Digital European Sky, which
leverages advanced digitalization, automation, and data-driven operations to optimize ATM while

• an analysis of ex ante control in terms of risk and efficiency;

5.2.2 Ex ante controls
Ex ante controls will remain important tools to help the SESAR 3 JU to prevent errors and to avoid the
need for ex post corrective actions. In accordance with Article 74 of the EU financial regulation and
Article 21 of the SESAR 3 JU’s financial rules, ‘each operation shall be subject at least to an ex ante
control relating to the operational and financial aspects of the operation, on the basis of a multiannual
control strategy which takes risk into account’. The main objective of ex ante controls, therefore, is to
ensure that the principle of sound financial management is applied. In 2026 and 2027, the following
ex ante activities will be systematically carried out:
• generating and checking grant agreements;
• initiating and verifying invoices for administrative expenditure;
• assessing periodic reports from grants and verifying and paying cost claims.
Additionally, the SESAR 3 JU will continue performing risk assessment at the project level during the
grant agreement preparation phase and before the signature of Horizon Europe grant agreements,
with due consideration to risks stemming from SMEs or newcomers.

5.2.3 Ex post controls
One of the other major pillars of assurance for the SESAR 3 JU is its ex post audit activity. Its main
objectives are as follows:
• providing the authorising officer with the necessary elements of assurance on the operational
expenditure in a timely manner;
• assessing the regularity and legality of the transactions;
• attaining residual error rates at an acceptable level at the closure of the Horizon Europe
programme, once the financial impact of all audits and correction and recovery measures
have been taken into account;
• determining the sound financial management of the transactions, with the support of the
internal or external technical experts, with the overall objective being to assess the value for
money of the SESAR 3 JU’s operations;
• identifying systemic errors through the analysis and synthesis of the results obtained and
formulating recommendations to address the issues;
• providing the SESAR 3 JU auditees with recommendations to improve the financial
management, processes, procedures and practices applied to the activities related to the
SESAR 3 JU’s contracts, with the main purpose being to ensure that recurring errors are
avoided by the SESAR 3 JU beneficiaries.
The Horizon Europe ex-post audit strategy is a risk based one, focusing on the riskier parts of the
population. Risk identification is based on robust risk assessments, triggered both by the Common
Audit Service (CAS) and by SESAR 3 JU. These risk-based audits allow the detection of errors that
cannot be identified by ex ante verifications and contribute substantially to the improved corrective
capacity, while ensuring appropriate audit coverage.
In 2026, the audit activity for SESAR 3 JU, will encompass 3 audits in 3 beneficiaries to be performed
by the CAS. For these activities, the SESAR 3 JU actively participates in the CAS coordination
mechanisms.
For 2027, the audits to be performed will be selected according to the risk profiles of beneficiaires on
cost claims submitted in 2026.
Furthermore, the new funding mechanism will require an adapted approach to ex-post financial
audits as well as technical reviews. These reviews, performed by external experts, focus on the
technical implementation of the action and are conducted ex-post (i.e. after an interim or final
payment). They concern the work of a single participant, and include the examination of non-financial
supporting documents demonstrating the proper technical implementation of the action. It remains
